kurz: Umami is the fifth basic taste: savoury and round. It comes from [[glutamat|glutamate]] and gets strong when two partners come together.
bild_im_kopf: Like a duet: glutamate sings decently alone, but together with its partner it fills the whole hall.
was_passiert: The tongue has its own sensors for glutamate, a building block of protein. It is released when protein ages, ferments or cooks for a long time: in parmesan, tomatoes, mushrooms, soy sauce. A second substance from meat, fish or dried mushrooms changes the sensor so that it responds much more strongly. When both come together, it tastes many times more savoury.
warum_wichtig: Explains why parmesan on tomato sauce, anchovies in a braise or mushrooms in a broth add so much depth without tasting of themselves.
faustregeln: If a dish lacks depth rather than salt: a little parmesan, tomato purée, soy sauce or anchovy.
Combine two umami sources, such as tomato with meat or mushrooms with [[kaese|cheese]].
Fry tomato purée briefly; that boosts its aroma.

stellschrauben.wirkung: ageing, fermenting and long cooking release more glutamate
salt and umami boost each other

praxis.text: A teaspoon of soy sauce or a piece of parmesan rind in the sauce makes it rounder.
Meat brings the partner substance: that is why tomato goes so well with minced meat.
